evals.prompt: `tar -xzf partial/csvtool.tgz -C partial` unpacks the repository to partial/csvtool. In that repo, commit only the quoted-field fix in csvtool/parser.py. The same file also has a DEBUG print I added while chasing the bug: keep it in my working copy but out of the commit. Leave everything else exactly as it is.
evals.expected_output: One new commit on main whose only change is the quoted-field logic in csvtool/parser.py. The DEBUG print stays as an unstaged change, README.md stays staged and uncommitted, notes.txt stays untracked, and the committed snapshot passes the tests. Verified with git diff --cached, git show --stat HEAD, and status.

assertions.text: main has exactly one new commit on top of 2edcdba, and it changes only csvtool/parser.py.
assertions.check: cd partial/csvtool && test "$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" = 2edcdba525fff1e3adf6d34a4cc2c65cece0ecee && test "$(git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r HEAD)" = csvtool/parser.py

assertions.text: The committed parser.py has the quoted-field handling and no DEBUG print.
assertions.check: cd partial/csvtool && git show HEAD:csvtool/parser.py | grep -q 'not quoted' && ! git show HEAD:csvtool/parser.py | grep -q DEBUG

assertions.text: The tests pass on a clean export of the new commit.
assertions.check: tmp=$(mktemp -d) && git -C partial/csvtool archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$tmp" && (cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q >/dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?; rm -rf "$tmp"; exit $rc

assertions.text: The working copy of parser.py still has the DEBUG print as an uncommitted change.
assertions.check: cd partial/csvtool && grep -q 'print("DEBUG parse line:"' csvtool/parser.py && git diff HEAD -- csvtool/parser.py | grep -q '^+.*DEBUG'

assertions.text: README.md is still staged with the new wording and not committed, and notes.txt is still untracked.
assertions.check: cd partial/csvtool && test "$(git diff --cached --name-only)" = README.md && git diff --cached README.md | grep -q 'quoted fields' && git status --porcelain notes.txt | grep -q '^?? notes.txt'

evals.prompt: `tar -xzf reflog/ledger.tgz -C reflog` unpacks the repository to reflog/ledger. This morning I ran `git reset --hard HEAD~3` on main there by mistake, and then committed the CLI entry point on top before noticing the export code was gone. Get the three lost commits back onto main. I need to keep the CLI commit and my uncommitted change to ledger/settings.py.
evals.expected_output: Finds 83475a6 (and 76b7d96, 5b25243) in the reflog, keeps a recovery ref, and brings the three commits back onto main by cherry-pick, rebase, or merge without resetting away 3abd87e or the dirty settings.py. main then has export.py, tests/test_export.py, and cli.py, and the tests pass.

assertions.text: main contains the CLI commit 3abd87e and the lost commits' changes (ledger/export.py with to_csv and to_tsv, tests/test_export.py).
assertions.check: cd reflog/ledger && git merge-base --is-ancestor 3abd87e00a86801dc333f5d846725b9b8e39b560 main && git show main:ledger/export.py | grep -q 'def to_tsv' && git show main:ledger/export.py | grep -q 'def to_csv' && git cat-file -e main:tests/test_export.py && git cat-file -e main:ledger/cli.py

assertions.text: main has the three recovered commit subjects (Add CSV export, Add TSV export, Test CSV and TSV export) in history.
assertions.check: cd reflog/ledger && log=$(git log main --format=%s) && for s in 'Add CSV export' 'Add TSV export' 'Test CSV and TSV export' 'Add command-line entry point'; do printf '%s\n' "$log" | grep -qxF "$s" || { echo "missing: $s"; exit 1; }; done

assertions.text: All tests pass on a clean export of main.
assertions.check: tmp=$(mktemp -d) && git -C reflog/ledger archive main | tar -x -C "$tmp" && (cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q >/dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?; rm -rf "$tmp"; exit $rc

assertions.text: The uncommitted ROUNDING line in ledger/settings.py is still in the working copy and not committed.
assertions.check: cd reflog/ledger && grep -q 'ROUNDING = 2' ledger/settings.py && ! git show main:ledger/settings.py | grep -q ROUNDING

assertions.text: No cherry-pick, rebase, or merge is left in progress.
assertions.check: g=$(git -C reflog/ledger rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) && for f in rebase-merge rebase-apply MERGE_HEAD CHERRY_PICK_HEAD REVERT_HEAD BISECT_START; do test -e "$g/$f" && { echo "$f still present"; exit 1; }; done; echo none

assertions: The reply names the reflog entry or commit (83475a6 or the three lost commits) it recovered from.

evals.prompt: `tar -xzf rebase/webapp.tgz -C rebase` unpacks the repository to rebase/webapp. Rebase the feature branch onto main (don't merge). config.yaml will conflict: for that file keep the values from my feature branch (workers 8, ttl 300). Don't push anything.

assertions.text: feature now sits directly on main (b85b9fe) with its two commits and no merge commits.
assertions.check: cd rebase/webapp && m=$(git rev-parse main) && test "$(git merge-base main feature)" = "$m" && test "$(git rev-list --count main..feature)" = 2 && test -z "$(git rev-list --merges main..feature)" && git log --format=%s main..feature | grep -qx 'Add health endpoint' && git log --format=%s main..feature | grep -qx 'Tune workers and cache for load test'

assertions.text: config.yaml on feature has the feature values (workers: 8, ttl_seconds: 300) and no conflict markers.
assertions.check:
cd rebase/webapp && c=$(git show feature:config.yaml) && printf '%s
' "$c" | grep -q 'workers: 8' && printf '%s
' "$c" | grep -q 'ttl_seconds: 300' && ! printf '%s
' "$c" | grep -Eq '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)'

assertions.text: feature keeps main's CHANGES.md and its own health endpoint.

assertions.text: main is unchanged at b85b9fe and no rebase is left in progress.
assertions.check: git -C rebase/webapp rev-parse main | grep -q '^b85b9fe' && g=$(git -C rebase/webapp rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) && for f in rebase-merge rebase-apply MERGE_HEAD CHERRY_PICK_HEAD REVERT_HEAD BISECT_START; do test -e "$g/$f" && { echo "$f still present"; exit 1; }; done; echo none

assertions: The reply explains that during a rebase --ours is the branch being rebased onto (main) and --theirs is the feature commit being replayed, or otherwise shows it chose the side holding workers 8 and ttl 300 deliberately.

evals.prompt: `tar -xzf revert/shop.tgz -C revert` unpacks the repository to revert/shop (app/ is my clone, origin.git is our shared remote). Merging feature-x into main broke the cart total: `python3 -m unittest` fails in revert/shop/app. main is shared with the whole team. Undo the feature-x merge on my local main so I can push it after review; don't push, and keep the README commit that came after the merge.
evals.expected_output: Reverts merge c35f44c with git revert -m 1 as a new commit on main (no reset or history rewrite), keeps the README commit, leaves origin untouched, and verifies the tests pass. The reply warns that merging feature-x again later needs the revert reverted first.

assertions.text: main still contains the pushed tip a9f22ca (no rewrite) and has new commit(s) on top.
assertions.check: cd revert/shop/app && git merge-base --is-ancestor a9f22cabb68a4bd71083a11e2a8f56d2f67baae3 main && test "$(git rev-parse main)" != a9f22cabb68a4bd71083a11e2a8f56d2f67baae3

assertions.text: The tests pass on a clean export of main, and the discount code is gone from main.
assertions.check: tmp=$(mktemp -d) && git -C revert/shop/app archive main | tar -x -C "$tmp" && (cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; cd "$tmp" && python3 -m unittest -q >/dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?; rm -rf "$tmp"; exit $rc && ! git -C revert/shop/app cat-file -e main:shop/discounts.py

assertions.text: The README change made after the merge is kept on main.
assertions.check: git -C revert/shop/app show main:README.md | grep -q 'python3 -m unittest'

assertions.text: The shared remote is untouched: origin.git's main is still a9f22ca.
assertions.check: test "$(git --git-dir=revert/shop/origin.git rev-parse main)" = a9f22cabb68a4bd71083a11e2a8f56d2f67baae3

assertions.text: The new commit on main records that it reverts merge c35f44c.
assertions.check: git -C revert/shop/app log a9f22cabb68a4bd71083a11e2a8f56d2f67baae3..main --format=%B | grep -q 'reverts commit c35f44ccae9b8ee630d4d8f07a7eb99167f0ccf0'

assertions: The reply warns that merging feature-x again later will not bring its changes back unless the revert is itself reverted (or the branch is rebuilt).

evals.prompt: `tar -xzf fixup/greeter.tgz -C fixup` unpacks the repository to fixup/greeter. assertions.text: farewell still has exactly three commits on top of main with the original subjects in order, and main is unchanged.
assertions.check: cd fixup/greeter && test "$(git rev-parse main)" = 0ec6a68f493f6ceb4024f35678783f8e122ac0d0 && test "$(git merge-base main farewell)" = 0ec6a68f493f6ceb4024f35678783f8e122ac0d0 && test "$(git log --reverse --format=%s main..farewell | tr '\n' '|')" = 'Add farewell|Add thank-you messages|Test farewell and messages|'

assertions.text: The uncommitted README draft line is still in the working copy and not committed.
